title: Task analysis: brushing, dressing, handwashing steps | ELUM
description: When "brush your teeth" is too much, break it down. Use task analysis to turn brushing, dressing and handwashing into action card steps, with examples.
keywords: task analysis, task analysis examples, brushing teeth steps, getting dressed steps, hand washing steps, breaking tasks into steps, ABA task analysis
heading: Task analysis: breaking routines into small steps
lede: A task that's hard to do all at once isn't something your child can't do. It just hasn't been broken down enough yet.

sections.heading: What is task analysis
paragraphs: Task analysis means breaking one task into small actions in order. For example, "wash your hands" becomes "turn on the water → add soap → rub → rinse → dry."

sections.heading: Tips for breaking it down well
list: Do it yourself as you write. If you only picture it in your head, you'll miss steps
Write actions you can see. "Rub the backs of your hands" instead of "get them clean"
One action per sentence. If you need "and," split it into two
Break down only the steps that get stuck. Steps your child does well can be combined
Start with 3 to 7 cards. If it's too long, split the routine in two

sections.heading: How far should you break it down
paragraphs: There's no single right answer. If your child can look at the card and start on their own, it's broken down enough. If they often stop at one card, try splitting just that card into two or three.
In ELUM, you can add cards, change the order and split a card into smaller steps right from the caregiver screen.

faq.q: How do I break down getting dressed?
faq.a: Make one card each in this order: underwear → top → pants → socks. If buttons or zippers are hard, give that part its own card.

faq.q: What if there are too many steps?
faq.a: Split the routine in two. For example, make 'getting ready in the morning' into separate 'washing up' and 'getting dressed' routines.
